what_happened: Job 20261107-110049-k8c2 ("Refuse readings that leave a structural request term undefined", code) failed in planning, before any code was written. In round 1 of 5 the critic said the reading misread the request. It then stopped the job with a plan that still needed revising. The request wants the origin fixed so the whole class is prevented. The reading narrowed that to a fixed list of four words (ladder, rung, tier, layer). The critic noted this narrowing but did not raise it as a plan finding, because the user had accepted the reading. The one major finding is that the planned matcher counts every occurrence of a listed word, including words that are only quoted from cited introspections. Athena's own generated root-cause requests quote them. This job's own request contains "(ladder, layer, tier, publish, and similar)". Under the plan, this job's own reading and every later request in the class would be refused unless it defined words it only quotes. Minor findings: the 3% refusal-share estimate is unmeasured and the plan ignores the in-loop replay that measures it. The list includes terms the repo already defines (ladder, rung) and common code words (layer, tier). Some step cross-references are wrong. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Nothing requires a new refusal rule's matcher to be run, at reading or planning time, over the real corpus of past requests before the critic sees it. This includes Athena's own generated root-cause requests, which quote the very terms the rule bans. The reading fixed a word list from one incident's wording, and the plan's tests use hand-picked shapes, so quoted mentions, terms the repo already defines, and ordinary code words never get tried. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step. A defect that running the matcher on real requests would show instead costs the whole planning spend. The reading also narrowed "prevent the whole class" to a short list, which the user accepted. The structural gap, a rule that is defined by listing words instead of by what the request actually uses undefined, was never raised before acceptance.
prevention: Before the planning critic runs on any job that adds or changes a reading-refusal or matching rule, run the draft matcher automatically over the corpus of real past requests, including Athena's generated root-cause requests, and over the job's own request. Put the match counts and the false-refusal list into the planner's input. Make a draft that refuses its own request, or refuses real requests that merely quote or cite a term, fail that check and go back to the planner as a mechanical finding, not wait for the critic to find it in a late round. Use that same corpus run to measure the refusal share so the estimate is not a guess.
proposed_request: Refuse readings that leave a structural request term undefined, so the whole class of undefined-term misreads is prevented. Outcome: when an accepted reading uses a structural term (such as ladder, rung, tier or layer) in a way that sets scope or ordering, and neither the reading nor the repo defines it, admission of the reading is refused with a message naming the term. Constraints: (1) A term that a request only quotes or cites, for example inside quotation marks or a parenthetical list drawn from a cited introspection, does not count as a use, so this job's own request and later generated root-cause requests are not refused. (2) Terms the repository already defines (check docs and the glossary) are not refused. (3) The check must run over the real corpus of past requests, with the match and refusal counts recorded, and the measured refusal share must be stated in the reading's replay declaration, not estimated. Acceptance: (a) a demonstration that runs the real gate on a request that quotes a listed word and is accepted; (b) a demonstration where an undefined structural use is refused; (c) a demonstration over the stored request corpus that shows zero refusals of ordinary requests, or lists each one; (d) a test that this job's own request passes the new rule. Update the CHANGELOG and docs/decisions.md in the same job.
